The remains were examined for taphonomic signatures of eagle predation. Our sample of nine individuals includes eight adult males with a mean estimated body mass of 22.2 ± 3.8 kg. We observed punctured orbits in two males, along with a raked scapula, two telling signs of eagle predation and/or feeding activity. One male was associated with a femur, enabling a body mass estimate of 21.8 kg. Postscript: in June 2026, we recovered the cranium and partial skeleton of an adult male with an estimated body mass of 26.2 kg; and again, we observed evidence of talon punctures and severe raking of the scapulae. Our findings are consistent with the depredations of Verreaux's eagles (Aquila verreauxii). If confirmed, the interaction exceeds the primate body-mass threshold deemed susceptible to avian predation, indicating that moderately large primates, including some hominins, may have experienced greater avian predation pressure than previously recognized.

title: The Wide Phenotypic Spectrum of Adult-Onset Single Large-Scale Mitochondrial DNA Deletion Syndromes.
abstract: Single large-scale mitochondrial DNA deletions (SLSMDs) give rise to a wide spectrum of clinical features, including Kearns-Sayre syndrome (KSS) and chronic progressive external ophthalmoplegia (CPEO). Because longitudinal data are scarce, the natural history remains poorly defined. This study was undertaken to describe the clinical spectrum in a large cohort of patients with clinical onset after 16 years of age. A retrospective multicenter study was performed in patients diagnosed and followed in seven European mitochondrial disease centers. Seventy patients were included. The median age at disease onset was 27 years, and the median age at last evaluation was 52 years, with a median follow-up duration of 19 years. Median survival from disease onset was 34 years. KSS spectrum disorder was present in 36% of the patients, while CPEO was identified in the remaining 64%. Among those with CPEO at onset, 27% progressed to KSS spectrum disorder. Multisystem involvement was present in 59%. The most frequently reported symptoms or signs were ptosis and/or ophthalmoplegia (100%), skeletal muscle weakness (56%), perceived fatigue (34%), visual impairment (30%), exercise intolerance (33%), pigmentary retinopathy (20%), hearing impairment (19%), cardiac conduction block (15%), ataxia (11%), epilepsy (14%), and cognitive impairment (11%). Our study gives further insight into the highly heterogenous clinical presentation and natural history associated with SLSMDs. The relevance of categorizing patients into classical syndromic phenotypes may be questioned, as the observed overlap in clinical manifestations and the frequent evolution of phenotype over time suggest a continuum of disease expression rather than clearly distinct syndromic entities.

title: Synthesis and Neurobiological Characterization of Barbamide and Analogs.
abstract: Marine cyanobacteria produce diverse secondary metabolites, which have biological activity on the human nervous system. We report evaluation of the cyanobacterial metabolite barbamide and analogs in the modulation of sensory neurons. We optimized synthesis of barbamide and an initial series of analogs with modifications of the trichloromethyl group to explore its role in function as well as simplify future synthetic efforts. Biological activity of this series was first evaluated using a multi-electrode array assay with human induced pluripotent stem cell nociceptors. We found that all three compounds were able to reduce neuronal firing rates in a dose-dependent manner consistent with potential use as an analgesic. Next, barbamide was further evaluated using primary human sensory neurons with whole cell patch clamp to gain insight into the mechanism driving the reduction in neuronal firing rate. We found that barbamide significantly decreased spontaneous and evoked action-potential firing in these neurons without overt toxicity. Finally, we evaluated the impact of barbamide on neurite outgrowth using PC12 cells and primary mouse dorsal root ganglia. We found that barbamide and trifluoromethyl barbamide increased neurite outgrowth. Together, this combination of effects further establishes the potential of the barbamide scaffold for the development of therapeutics focused on neuronal function/dysfunction.

title: Metabolomics Profiling of Serum Small Extracellular Vesicle-Enriched Fractions Across Early Post-Injury Intervals Following Severe Traumatic Brain Injury.
abstract: Severe traumatic brain injury (sTBI) induces metabolic disturbances that remain difficult to assess non-invasively. This exploratory study compared metabolomics profiles of serum small extracellular vesicle-enriched fractions from healthy controls and patients with sTBI sampled at days 1, 3, and 5 post-injury. Using high-resolution liquid chromatography-mass spectrometry (LC-MS), we identified metabolite differences associated with each sampled post-injury interval. Principal component analysis showed group-level separation between controls and the individual post-injury interval groups, with the largest separation observed in the day 1 comparison. N-Acetyl-l-aspartic acid, a canonical marker of neuronal integrity, showed lower abundance in the day 1 group relative to controls, whereas PGF2α ethanolamide showed lower abundance relative to controls in all three interval-specific comparisons. Glu-ser and tryptophan also met the differential-abundance criteria in more than one interval vs. control comparison. Ingenuity pathway analysis (IPA) linked the day 1 metabolite alterations to literature-curated neurological functions, including demyelination and neurodegeneration; however, these associations are presented as hypothesis-generating. Collectively, these findings identify serum small extracellular vesicle-enriched fraction metabolite alterations associated with sTBI for further investigation in fully longitudinal sTBI cohorts.

title: Preliminary Assessment of Exploratory Behavior in Rats with Lifelong Absence of Brain Serotonin Using an RFID-Controlled Social Home-Cage Access Platform.
abstract: Lifelong central serotonin deficiency affects behavioral development, yet its impact on spontaneous exploratory and engagement-related behavior in a social-housing context remains incompletely characterized. To address this gap, we studied adolescent male Tryptophan Hydroxylase 2 knockout (Tph2-KO) rats using two complementary automated approaches: a radio-frequency identification (RFID)-controlled Social RatPad access platform connected to a social home-cage compartment and the LABORAS behavioral profiling system. In the Social RatPad platform, the central cage served as the shared living environment, whereas the automated components controlled individual access to the touchscreen-equipped testing chambers and logged RFID-identified events. Following RFID implantation, adolescent male Dark Agouti Tph2-KO and wild-type (WT) littermate rats were monitored in the Social RatPad/RFID platform and tested individually in LABORAS during two standardized 2 h sessions. The present analysis focuses on spontaneous corridor use, chamber access, touchscreen trial initiation, and free-moving exploratory behavior; touchscreen accuracy and cognitive learning outcomes were not used as inferential endpoints. KO rats showed reduced early exploratory activation in LABORAS, delayed onset of voluntary touchscreen interaction, descriptively lower visual-discrimination trial engagement, and more heterogeneous access patterns across animals. LABORAS differences were most evident during initial exposure and attenuated during the second session. These findings suggest that lifelong absence of central serotonin alters the initiation and organization of spontaneous exploratory and engagement-related behavior during adolescence. The results also show that Social RatPad/RFID and LABORAS measurements provide complementary, but not directly interchangeable, information because they differ in duration, social context, and novelty/familiarity of the testing environment.

title: Aβ Aggregate-Gated Ratiometric Probe Reveals Peri-Plaque Acidification Arising from Lysosomal Dysfunction in Alzheimer's Disease.
abstract: Alzheimer's disease (AD) is characterized by amyloid-β (Aβ) plaques surrounded by plaque-associated dystrophic neurites (PADNs), where dysfunctional autolysosomal vesicles accumulate abundantly. However, whether Aβ-induced autolysosomal dysfunction contributes to remodeling of the plaque microenvironment remains unclear. Herein, we developed DQ, an Aβ aggregate-gated ratiometric fluorescent probe in which recognition of fibrillar Aβ activates pH-responsive fluorescence. This target-triggered sensing strategy restricts pH reporting to the vicinity of Aβ aggregates, enabling selective visualization of local plaque-associated microenvironments with minimal background interference. DQ exhibited high selectivity toward fibrillar Aβ and enabled imaging of local pH changes in both cellular models and transgenic AD mice. Using DQ, we revealed progressive acidification surrounding plaques during AD progression and demonstrated an age-dependent increase in peri-plaque acidification. Furthermore, imaging analyses showed that local acidification was closely associated with lysosomal dysfunction within PADNs. Mechanistic studies further demonstrated that autolysosomal impairment within PADNs causes lysosomal proton leakage and microenvironmental acidification. Repair of lysosomal dysfunction alleviated multiple AD-associated pathological features, including plaque burden, neuroinflammation, synaptic loss, and cognitive impairment. Collectively, this work establishes a target-gated ratiometric sensing strategy for spatially resolved interrogation of plaque-associated microenvironments and identifies PADN-associated lysosomal proton dysregulation as an important pathological event in AD progression.

title: Advances in Fluorescent Probes to Illuminate Chloride Dynamics in the Brain.
abstract: Chloride ions (Cl-) play an important role in regulating neuronal excitability, inhibitory neurotransmission, cell volume control, and ionic homeostasis in the brain. Precise control of the intracellular chloride concentration is essential for normal neuronal and glial function, while its dysregulation has been linked to neurological disorders such as epilepsy, neurodevelopmental disorders, schizophrenia, and neurodegenerative diseases. Therefore, understanding chloride dynamics has become an essential step in neuroscience research. To further support the observation of chloride dynamics, fluorescence imaging has emerged as a powerful approach for monitoring intracellular chloride in living cells, offering high spatial and temporal resolution that complements conventional electrophysiological techniques. This review provides an overview of the significance of chloride dynamics in the nervous system and discusses fluorescence-based strategies for investigating chloride homeostasis. The development of fluorescent chloride probes is summarized, from early small-molecule dyes to genetically encoded fluorescent proteins with emphasis on their sensing mechanisms, advantages, limitations, and applications. Finally, current challenges and future directions in probe development, including improved chloride selectivity, reduced pH sensitivity, and subcellular targeting, are discussed.

title: Dopamine D1 Receptor on Vasoactive Intestinal Polypeptide-Expressing Interneurons in the Orbitofrontal Cortex Regulates Spatial Working Memory Acquisition in Mice.
abstract: GABAergic vasoactive intestinal polypeptide-positive (VIP+) interneurons represent a primary interneuron subclass in the cortex, known for their disinhibitory role in local microcircuits, their regulation of sensory gain, and their modulation of goal-oriented learning. The orbitofrontal cortex (OFC) is essential for decision-making and functions as a key node in the dopamine-mediated reward pathway. To investigate the importance of dopamine signaling in OFC VIP+ interneurons during working memory, we evaluated the role of the dopamine D1 receptor (D1R). We found that cell-type-specific knockdown of D1R did not alter the basal activity of VIP+ interneurons or the general behavior of mice. However, this knockdown compromised the D1R-mediated regulation of VIP+ neuronal output. Notably, the deficit of D1R in the VIP+ interneurons of the OFC specifically impaired the acquisition of working memory in the reward-alternation T-maze test.

title: Effects of Constitutive Depletion or Excess of Serotonin during Development on the Maturation of Prefrontal Monoaminergic Circuits.
abstract: Serotonin (5-hydroxytryptamine; 5-HT) is a critical neuromodulatory morphogen-like signal that governs prenatal cortical circuit assembly, and altered 5-HT signaling is implicated in a wide range of psychiatric disorders. Yet the structural consequences of lifelong 5-HT imbalance during the initial blueprinting phase remain poorly defined. Here, we used two genetic rat models representing the extremes of 5-HT homeostasis, Tph2 knockout (Tph2-/-; chronic depletion of 5-HT) and 5-HTT knockout (5-HTT-/-; chronic excess of 5-HT), to investigate sub-region-specific alterations in the embryonic medial prefrontal cortex (mPFC) and in prefrontal monoaminergic circuit maturation. Our results demonstrate that the developing mPFC is not uniformly vulnerable to 5-HT dysregulation. Instead, the prelimbic (PL) cortex emerged as a region of heightened sensitivity to low 5-HT levels, exhibiting localized hyperinnervation of catecholaminergic fibers and an increase in deep-layer Tbr1+ neurons. In contrast, within the infralimbic (IL) cortex, 5-HT deficiency induced a selective loss of reelin (Reln)-producing Cajal-Retzius (CR) cells, indicating a sub-region-specific disruption of the cortical scaffold. Transcriptomic analyses identified selective upregulation of the low-affinity monoamine transporter Slc29a4 and the monoamine oxidase A (Maoa) in 5-HTT-/- embryos, suggesting activation of compensatory extracellular 5-HT clearance pathways during embryogenesis. Together, these findings establish prenatal 5-HT levels as an essential determinant of afferent innervation and cortical scaffold integrity, and suggest that late-gestational developmental blueprinting errors may provide a neurodevelopmental substrate for later monoaminergic circuit dysfunction linked to social and cognitive phenotypes.

title: DNA Damage-Induced Senescence Reshapes Transcriptomic and Functional Landscape of Human Neural Progenitor Cells.
abstract: Ageing-related decline in hippocampal neurogenesis has been associated with cognitive impairment and neurodegenerative disease, yet experimentally tractable human models to study the underlying cellular and molecular mechanisms remain limited. Cellular senescence has emerged as a candidate driver of age-related tissue dysfunction, but its induction and consequences in human NPCs have not been well characterized. Here, we established a human in vitro model of NPC senescence using induced pluripotent stem cell-derived NPCs exposed to transient low-dose doxorubicin to induce genotoxic stress while minimizing acute cytotoxicity. Doxorubicin-treated NPCs developed a persistent senescence-associated phenotype characterized by increased senescence-associated β-galactosidase activity, reduced proliferation, persistent DNA damage and sustained induction of p21 and p16. Transcriptomic profiling revealed widespread senescence-associated remodelling, including enrichment of p53-associated and inflammatory programs and repression of cell cycle and DNA repair pathways. Dox-treated NPCs exhibited limited apoptotic response despite transcriptional priming of apoptotic pathways and underwent mitochondrial remodelling characterized by altered respiratory coupling and increased ATP-linked respiration. In parallel, they acquired a senescence-associated secretory phenotype enriched in inflammatory, TGFβ-related and pro-angiogenic factors and conditioned media from these cells promoted angiogenesis in vascular organoids. Importantly, key senescence-associated features were recapitulated in human hippocampal organoids, demonstrating that the phenotype extends beyond the 2D NPC model to a three-dimensional neural context. Together, these findings establish a tractable human model of genotoxic stress-induced NPC senescence and support a role for senescence-associated changes in linking genotoxic stress to altered progenitor function, mitochondrial remodelling and paracrine niche remodelling relevant to hippocampal ageing and neurodegeneration.

title: Associations Between Sexual Goals, Relationship Satisfaction, and Conflict Among Couples Affected by Sexual Interest/Arousal Disorder.
abstract: Engaging in sex to pursue approach goals (e.g., intimacy), is linked with greater relationship satisfaction, whereas avoidance goals (e.g., preventing partner disappointment) relate to lower satisfaction and higher conflict. Compared to those without sexual difficulties, individuals with Sexual Interest/Arousal Disorder (SIAD) report fewer approach and more avoidance goals, with potential implications for their relationship quality. To examine bidirectional associations between partner-focused sexual goals and relationship satisfaction and conflict, individuals with SIAD and their partners (N = 263 couples) completed validated measures at baseline and 6 months later. Guided by the actor-partner interdependence model, structural equation models revealed that higher approach goals among individuals with SIAD were associated with greater concurrent relationship satisfaction. In contrast, partners' higher avoidance goals were associated with lower concurrent satisfaction and higher conflict for both couple members. Prospective associations indicated that sexual goals did not predict 6-month outcomes, or vice versa, except that those individuals with SIAD who reported higher baseline relationship satisfaction reported lower avoidance goals 6 months later. Findings highlight that sexual goals mostly relate to proximal experiences of relationship quality in couples facing SIAD, suggesting that promoting approach and reducing avoidance goals may be linked to more favorable outcomes in their sexual relationships.

title: Aβ42 induces selective degeneration in hippocampal cells of aged monkeys.
abstract: The hippocampus is one of the earliest and most severely affected brain regions in Alzheimer's disease (AD) and is critical for memory formation. However, the precise mechanisms through which AD disrupts hippocampal neurons remain poorly understood. To investigate the effects of Aβ42 in a model closer to humans, we performed stereotaxic injections of an adeno-associated virus serotype 9 (AAV9) vector encoding human Aβ42 into the hippocampus of young (7-year-old) and aged (>20-year-old) cynomolgus monkeys. We found that AAV9-mediated Aβ42 expression induced more severe neuropathology, reduced daytime activity, and increased sleep disturbances in aged monkeys compared to young controls. Single-nucleus RNA sequencing (snRNA-seq) revealed an age-dependent reduction in disease-associated microglia subtype II (DAM II) in the aged hippocampus. Furthermore, we identified a specific subtype of hippocampal pyramidal neurons (PCs) ( TRPS1 + RELN +) that is selectively vulnerable to Aβ42 toxicity in aged monkeys. Our findings indicate that Aβ42 toxicity is exacerbated in the aged primate hippocampus due to a combination of microglial decline and the selective vulnerability of a distinct neuronal subtype ( TRPS1 + RELN + PCs). This identified subtype represents a new potential therapeutic target for treating hippocampal dysfunction in AD.

title: Early Treatment with Oral Pirfenidone Improves Bladder Function after Contusive Spinal Cord Injury in Mice.
journal: American journal of physiology. Renal physiology
abstract: Spinal cord injury (SCI) disrupts innervation to the lower urinary tract, resulting in bladder dysfunction that predisposes to urinary infections and renal impairment. While inflammation is central to bladder pathology after SCI, the molecular events linking acute to chronic remodeling are poorly defined. We hypothesized that early treatment with pirfenidone, an anti-inflammatory and anti-fibrotic drug, would attenuate bladder pathology after SCI. Adult female C57BL/6J mice underwent contusive SCI or sham laminectomy, and bladders were collected at 2, 7, 16, and 45 days later. SCI induced bladder hypertrophy, edema, hemorrhage, neutrophil infiltration, cell proliferation and loss of voiding function in the first 48 hours. Transcriptomic profiling at this timepoint was characterized by activation of inflammatory and cytokine pathways including TNF-α, IL-6, the complement cascade, and TGFβ. Although bladder function partially recovered by day 7, inflammatory pathways persisted and extracellular matrix (ECM) remodeling programs emerged. By day 16, robust activation of ECM-remodeling pathways was evident in all bladders. Treatment with pirfenidone during the acute inflammatory phase (day 2-7) reduced bladder hypertrophy and suppressed expression of pro-fibrotic, inflammatory, and neuroplasticity-associated genes including Bdnf and Chrm2 that encodes muscarinic receptor 2 (M2). Mechanistically, pirfenidone attenuated TGFb signaling as shown by downregulation of phosphoSmad2 protein in whole bladders and decreased M2 receptor expression in the urothelium. These molecular changes correlated with improved function in pirfenidone-treated mice as shown by fewer voiding events with larger urine volumes up until 45 days after SCI. Early treatment with pirfenidone limits inflammation and fibrosis, normalizes neural signaling, and improves bladder function after SCI.

title: B 1 + Optimization in the Heart at 7 T.
abstract: At 7 T, the short RF wavelength in tissue (∼11 cm) causes destructive interference within the chest, leading to B 1 + inhomogeneity and posing a critical challenge for cardiac MRI and MRS. While subject-specific parallel-transmit (pTx) optimization can mitigate this, it requires calibration scans and offline computation. To simplify this process, a static "global" shim was calculated and demonstrated to outperform the default transmit configuration without participant-specific calibration. B 1 + maps were acquired in 12 healthy volunteers at 7 T using an 8-channel 1H torso coil. "Personal" phase-only shims were calculated per subject by minimizing a cost function of B 1 + homogeneity and efficiency. The "global" shim was calculated by optimizing performance across the cohort, then validated in six additional volunteers by comparing performance against the native mode. In the validation cohort, the "global" significantly outperformed the native shim. It increased the Mean Transmit Sensitivity by ∼20% and reduced CoV by ∼ 16 % in the septum. The fixed global shim performance was within 3% of the computationally expensive personal shim for all metrics. A fixed, population-derived, global phase shim provides a practical, calibration-free approach for improving cardiac B 1 + performance at 7 T. The present results extend previous universal RF-shimming work through prospective evaluation in an independent validation cohort and demonstrate that much of the benefit of personal shimming can be retained without participant-specific optimization. The resulting fixed-phase configuration could also provide a practical route towards implementation on single-transmit hardware for cardiac imaging and spectroscopic applications.

title: Painful Non-Diabetic Lumbosacral Radiculoplexus Neuropathy Following Tirzepatide Exposure: A Case Report.
journal: Journal of the peripheral nervous system : JPNS
abstract: Lumbosacral radiculoplexus neuropathy (LRPN) is an uncommon neuropathic syndrome occurring predominantly in patients with diabetes mellitus, although non-diabetic forms are increasingly recognized. Rare peripheral neuropathies have been reported during glucagon-like peptide-1 receptor agonist (GLP-1 receptor agonist [GLP-1RA]) therapy; however, LRPN has not previously been described in this clinical context, particularly in non-diabetic individuals. We describe a well-characterized case of painful non-diabetic LRPN developing following a period of rapid metabolic shift during tirzepatide therapy. A 62-year-old man previously treated with tirzepatide for weight loss developed, approximately 8 weeks after discontinuation, acute left-sided low back pain, rapidly progressing to severe neuropathic pain, distal weakness, and sensory loss. MR neurography demonstrated enlargement and contrast enhancement of the left L5 nerve root and sciatic nerve, associated with denervation edema. Electrophysiological studies demonstrated an axonal process consistent with lumbosacral radiculoplexus neuropathy, while cerebrospinal fluid analysis showed albuminocytological dissociation. Classical diabetic-related plexopathy was excluded by normal glucose values; an extensive work-up excluded infectious, neoplastic, paraneoplastic, and systemic inflammatory causes. The patient was treated with intravenous methylprednisolone followed by an oral corticosteroid taper and intensive rehabilitation. At 8-month follow-up, neuropathic pain had completely resolved and plantar flexion had recovered, whereas severe foot dorsiflexion weakness persisted, and the patient walked with a single crutch and an ankle-foot orthosis, consistent with the expected outcome of severe axonal lumbosacral radiculoplexus neuropathy. Tirzepatide exposure was associated with rapid weight loss in a normoglycaemic individual. This case highlights a severe non-diabetic lumbosacral radiculoplexus neuropathy following a period of rapid metabolic shift during GLP-1RA therapy. Although causality cannot be established, the temporal association and clinical context raise the hypothesis that abrupt metabolic changes may act as a permissive factor for immune-mediated lumbosacral plexus injury in susceptible individuals.

title: Pericyte PDGFR-β deficiency contributes to Aβ pathology through impaired glymphatic transport and altered AQP-4 localization.
journal: Alzheimer's & dementia : the journal of the Alzheimer's Association
abstract: Pericyte platelet-derived growth factor receptor-β (PDGFR-β) signaling maintains neurovascular integrity, but its role in glymphatic function is unknown. We investigated whether pericyte PDGFR-β deficiency is associated with glymphatic dysfunction and altered aquaporin-4 (AQP-4) localization in Alzheimer's disease (AD). Glymphatic trafficking was assessed by fluorescent cerebrospinal fluid (CSF) tracer injection. Meningeal lymphatic drainage was blocked by deep cervical lymph node (dcLN) ligation. Pericyte coverage, AQP-4 expression/localization, and basement membrane components were analyzed by immunofluorescence and western blot. Pericyte-conditioned medium was used to examine the effects of pericyte-derived factors on astrocytic AQP-4. The AQP-4 facilitator TGN-073 was administered to assess functional rescue. Blood-brain barrier integrity, microvascular density, and cerebral blood flow were also evaluated. DcLN ligation impaired amyloid beta clearance and spatial memory. Both APP/PS1 and Pdgfr-β+/- mice exhibited pericyte loss and glymphatic dysfunction, with Pdgfr-β+/- mice additionally showing reduced perivascular AQP-4 expression, accompanied by decreased laminin-α2/β1. In vitro, pericyte-derived factors promoted AQP-4 expression. TGN-073 partially improved small-molecule CSF tracer distribution in Pdgfr-β+/- mice. Pdgfr-β+/-/APP/PS1 mice displayed exacerbated AD-like pathology. PDGFR-β deficiency compromises basement membrane integrity and AQP-4 localization, impairing glymphatic transport and accelerating AD pathogenesis. The PDGFR-β pathway may represent a novel therapeutic target for enhancing waste clearance.

title: Concept, content, and face validity of a self-assessment index for integral brain health - an international modified e-Delphi study.
journal: Alzheimer's & dementia : the journal of the Alzheimer's Association
abstract: Commonly used brain health assessments rely on elevated levels of skill and address only one brain health domain. A modified e-Delphi of 17 international experts considered the concept, content, and face validity and dimensionality of Hachinski's proposal to combine self-assessed cognitive, psychological, and social domains of brain health. A moderator shared anonymized results with panelists, informing input on each round. A generative and three additional rounds reached consensus. Three questions included cognitive (how is your mind working), psychological (how is your mood), and social health (how are your social relationships). Each item has a five-point descriptor (much worse, a bit worse, the same, a bit better, much better) for time set by clinical or study relevance and repeated at follow-up. This study establishes the concept, content, and face validity of a self-assessed Integral Brain Health Index, offering a framework for construct validity, reliability, predictive validity, and clinical usefulness.

title: Network architecture of sleep, biomarkers, and cognition: Rapid eye movement sleep latency as a cross-domain connector.
journal: Alzheimer's & dementia : the journal of the Alzheimer's Association
abstract: Sleep disturbances are linked to Alzheimer's disease (AD) and related dementias (ADRD) pathology and cognitive decline, but how sleep architecture, biomarkers, and cognition are organized within a conditional dependence framework remains unclear. We studied 98 adults spanning normal cognition (NC; n = 21), mild cognitive impairment (MCI; n = 34), and clinically diagnosed AD dementia (n = 43) using overnight polysomnography, plasma phosphorylated tau181 (p-tau181), neurofilament light chain (NfL), brain-derived neurotrophic factor (BDNF), amyloid-β positron emission tomography (PET), and multidomain cognitive testing. A regularized Gaussian graphical model was used to characterize conditional associations and identify cross-domain connectivity among sleep, biomarkers, and cognition. The 17-variable network contained 26 edges, with significantly denser within-domain than cross-domain connectivity (40.5% vs 9.6%; p < 0.001). Direct sleep-cognition connections were sparse. Rapid eye movement (REM) sleep latency had the highest bridge strength (0.387), directly connecting the sleep domain with NfL, amyloid-β PET, and BDNF. Plasma p-tau181 was the only biomarker directly connected to global cognition. Exploratory mediation analyses were consistent with indirect associations involving p-tau181 in three of five cognitive domains. Sleep architecture and cognition were conditionally linked primarily through biomarker nodes. REM sleep latency and plasma p-tau181 may represent key cross-domain connectors linking sleep architecture, neurodegeneration, and cognition across the AD continuum.

title: Apolipoprotein E genotype, PET and MRI biomarkers, and vascular risk: A multi-modal investigation of memory performance in US POINTER.
journal: Alzheimer's & dementia : the journal of the Alzheimer's Association
abstract: The apolipoprotein E (APOE) ε4 allele is a key genetic risk factor for Alzheimer's disease (AD), but the etiology of impairment in non-carriers is less understood. We used regression and mediation models to test the cross-sectional relationships among APOE genotype, positron emission tomography amyloid and tau, vascular risk factors, and episodic memory within the US Study to Protect Brain Health Through Lifestyle Intervention to Reduce Risk ancillary imaging dataset of non-demented older adults. In our cohort (N = 880), APOE ε4 carriers showed higher global amyloid, higher meta-temporal tau, smaller hippocampal volume, poorer memory, and a stronger relationship between amyloid and tau standardized uptake value ratio (SUVR; ∆β = 0.22, p < 0.001). Tau predicted memory (p < 0.01) and partially mediated the APOE-memory association. In a stratified analysis, higher Framingham Heart Study risk score (FHS; p = 0.022) and not tau SUVR (p = 0.1) were associated with memory among APOE ε4 non-carriers, whereas tau SUVR (p = 0.048) but not FHS risk score (p = 0.55) was associated with memory amongst APOE ε4 carriers. Drivers of cognitive performance appear to be specific to APOE ε4 carrier status, emphasizing the need to identify alternative, or contributing, disease mechanisms among non-carriers. The US Study to Protect Brain Health Through Lifestyle Intervention to Reduce Risk (U.S. POINTER) cohort is composed of older adults at elevated risk of cognitive decline and cardiovascular disease burden. Further multimodal neuroimaging data was collected through the POINTER Imaging ancillary study. At baseline evaluation, the apolipoprotein E (APOE) ε4 genotype was significantly associated with amyloid and tau pathology, hippocampal atrophy, and poor episodic memory performance. APOE ε4 genotype stratification analysis showed significant associations of Framingham cardiovascular risk score and smoking status with memory in non-carriers only. Etiological pathways of dementia may differ in contributive strength to cognitive deterioration within this at-risk cohort.

title: [Effect of sustained-release gelatin methacryloyl hydrogel microspheres loaded with neural stem cells and neurotrophin 3 for repairing spinal cord injury in rats].
journal: Zhongguo xiu fu chong jian wai ke za zhi = Zhongguo xiufu chongjian waike zazhi = Chinese journal of reparative and reconstructive surgery
abstract: To construct sustained-release gelatin methacryloyl (GelMA) hydrogel microspheres loaded with neural stem cells (NSCs) and neurotrophin 3 (NT-3), and to investigate their roles and underlying mechanisms in spinal cord injury (SCI) repair through both in vitro and in vivo experiments. Hydrogels with different degrees of methacrylation (GelMA-30, GelMA-60, GelMA-PR) containing NT-3, as well as GelMA-30 hydrogel microspheres, were prepared. Their micromorphology and pore size were characterized by scanning electron microscopy; porosity, swelling ratio, in vitro degradation, and sustained-release capacity were measured for material characterization. NSCs from Sprague-Dawley (SD) rats were co-cultured with hydrogels of varying methacrylation degrees, concentrations, or morphological forms. Cell compatibility was assessed using the cell counting kit 8 (CCK-8) and live/dead cell staining. Based on uniform pore structure, moderate swelling ratio, in vitro release performance, and cell viability, the optimal hydrogel material for NSCs loading was selected for subsequent experiments. In vitro, NSCs without hydrogel were served as the control group. The effects of the prepared hydrogel/microspheres on NSCs proliferation, apoptosis, and differentiation were evaluated by EdU staining, propidium iodide (PI) staining, Annexin Ⅴ/PI staining, and immunostaining for neural differentiation markers-glial fibrillary acidic protein (GFAP), myelin basic protein (MBP), and neuronal class Ⅲ β-tubulin (TUJ-1). Forty 8-week-old female SD rats were randomly divided into sham-operation, SCI, hydrogel, and microsphere groups. The sham-operation group underwent only laminectomy without spinal cord injury; the other groups received T10 SCI modeling, after which the hydrogel and microsphere groups received a 10 μL transplantation of the respective hydrogel into the lesion area. Within 8 weeks after operation, the Basso-Beattie-Bresnahan (BBB) scale was assessed weekly to evaluate motor function recovery, and footprint analysis was performed at 8 weeks. Spinal cord tissues were harvested for histological and immunofluorescence staining (GFAP, MBP, TUJ-1, Ki67) to assess the effects on motor function and neural regeneration/repair. Expressions of GFAP, MBP, and TUJ-1 were detected by Western blot and real-time fluorescence quantitative PCR (qRT-PCR). Furthermore, transcriptome sequencing was performed to compare gene expression differences between the hydrogel and microsphere groups. Scanning electron microscopy showed that all hydrogels possessed porous structures, with the microspheres exhibiting larger pore sizes and higher porosity and swelling ratios than the other hydrogels. In vitro experiments demonstrated that all materials maintained stable mass within 28 days and had favorable sustained-release profiles, with the microspheres reaching a cumulative release rate of 90% at 5 days. Cell compatibility assays revealed that NSCs remained highly viable in all hydrogels, and the 5.0%GelMA-30 microspheres showed the highest cell viability (P<0.05). Based on these material characterizations, the 5.0%GelMA-30 hydrogel/microspheres were selected for further experiments. In vitro experiment showed that, compared with the hydrogel group, the microsphere group exhibited superior promotion of NSCs proliferation and differentiation toward neurons and oligodendrocytes, while more effectively inhibiting astrocytic differentiation (P<0.05). In vivo experiments indicated that both the hydrogel and microsphere groups promoted motor function recovery in SCI rats, with the microsphere group showing significantly better recovery (P<0.05). Histological analysis revealed a smaller cavitation area in the microsphere group than in the hydrogel group, and Ki67 staining further confirmed stronger NSCs proliferative activity in the microsphere group (P<0.05). Western blot and qRT-PCR results were consistent, showing that the microsphere group enhanced neural and myelin regeneration and inhibited glial scar formation (P<0.05). Transcriptome sequencing analysis revealed more differentially expressed genes in the microsphere group compared with the hydrogel group, with 74 upregulated and 31 downregulated genes, suggesting that the sustained-release hydrogel microspheres may exert their reparative effects during SCI repair through regulation of multiple gene expressions. The GelMA-30 sustained-release hydrogel microspheres exhibit good biocompatibility and sustained drug release performance. They promote structural repair and functional recovery after SCI by regulating multiple gene expressions.

title: Circulating MicroRNAs as Biomarkers in Post-Traumatic Stress Disorder and Related Psychiatric Disorders: Epigenetic Insights and Therapeutic Potential.
abstract: Post-Traumatic Stress Disorder (PTSD)-affecting approximately 5-10% of the general population and up to 15% in trauma-exposed groups-is a debilitating mental health condition triggered by life-threatening events, often causing extreme fear or helplessness. Circulating microRNAs (miRNAs), non-coding RNAs in body fluids, are emerging as non-invasive biomarkers for central nervous system (CNS) disorders due to their role in epigenetic regulation of gene expression. Over the past two decades, miRNA dysregulation has been implicated in psychiatric disorders, including PTSD, Major Depressive Disorder (MDD), Bipolar Disorder (BD), and schizophrenia (SZ), with shared features like cognitive impairment. This review showcases recent advances in miRNA dysregulation across these disorders, highlighting their potential as diagnostic tools and therapeutic targets. This review explores miRNA-mediated epigenetic mechanisms, including transgenerational effects and glucocorticoid signaling, as novel avenues for biomarker development and therapeutic intervention in PTSD and related disorders. By integrating molecular, clinical, and translational perspectives, we evaluate miRNAs' roles in PTSD pathogenesis, their ability to cross the blood-brain barrier, and their modulation of inflammatory and neurotrophic pathways. miRNA-based therapeutics, including miRNA mimics, anti-miRs, and exosome-mediated delivery systems, are emerging as promising interventions for restoring neuroplasticity, normalizing glucocorticoid signaling, and reducing neuroinflammation in these disorders. Despite their promise, challenges such as standardized detection methods and variable expression across body fluids persist. This review underscores the potential of circulating miRNAs in precision psychiatry, advocating for larger cohort studies and improved profiling to enhance clinical applicability.

title: Basal Forebrain Projections to the Lateral Habenula Regulate Ethanol and Sucrose Consumption.
abstract: The lateral habenula (LHb) receives afferent input from various basal forebrain (BF) regions known for their role in aversion-related behaviors, depression, and addiction. However, little is known about the role of this circuitry in ethanol consumption, including in the presence of aversive stimuli. Here, we assessed the role of BF input to the LHb in alcohol and sucrose consumption using a chemogenetic approach. Following long-term intermittent alcohol access (IAA) or control conditions, male and female Long-Evans rats underwent surgery for the expression of designer receptors in BF-to-LHb projections. We then excited this pathway in rats with IAA history or inhibited this pathway in rats with limited ethanol history before testing consumption of ethanol and natural reward both in the presence and absence of quinine adulteration. Long-term IAA elevated ethanol drinking in all rats, and enhanced ethanol preference with and without quinine adulteration in males. Chemogenetic activation of BF-to-LHb neurons in rats with IAA history produced different effects in males and females: excitation enhanced ethanol intake in females, but reduced ethanol preference in males, regardless of quinine adulteration. Activation also led to a relative insensitivity to quinine adulteration of sucrose when compared to controls, particularly in females. Chemogenetic inhibition in rats with limited ethanol history did not alter consumption of ethanol or sucrose, with or without quinine adulteration. Our results suggest a role for BF-to-LHb circuitry in ethanol drinking that may vary based on sex, and a potential role for this circuitry in the sensitivity to quinine when combined with natural reward.

title: Growth Differentiation Factor 15 as a Body-Brain Stress Signal in Major Depression and Insulin Resistance.
abstract: Major depressive disorder (MDD) is linked to insulin resistance, which is associated with increased risk, chronicity, and poor treatment response in depression. Growth differentiation factor 15 (GDF15), a stress-induced cytokine linking peripheral to central energy metabolism, may mediate this link, but its role in MDD is unclear. The authors assessed associations of MDD and insulin resistance with GDF15; links between GDF15, symptoms, and stress; and whether baseline GDF15 levels predict symptom persistence. In this preregistered secondary analysis, 190 participants with MDD and 183 control participants provided blood, underwent interviews, and completed questionnaires. GDF15 values were log-transformed and analyzed with linear models. The association between GDF15 and depression severity was validated in an independent cohort of medication-free MDD patients (N=168). Both MDD diagnosis and insulin resistance were significantly associated with elevated GDF15 (adjusted for age and sex). Across all participants, elevated GDF15 was significantly associated with greater depressive severity, childhood trauma, and perceived stress. In stratified analyses, the association with depression severity and perceived stress was significant only in healthy control subjects. In MDD patients, baseline GDF15 was associated with persistence of symptoms across time. In the second independent sample of medication-free MDD patients, depression severity was significantly associated with GDF15. GDF15 is elevated in MDD and insulin resistance, indicating convergent stress-energy pathway activation, and in MDD higher GDF15 predicted symptom persistence. These findings position GDF15 as a mechanistic biomarker at the interface of psychiatric and metabolic health and reinforce the need for integrated care of metabolic and mental health.

title: Exercise intensity and testosterone modulate cognitive recovery and BDNF levels during morphine abstinence in castrated male rats.
abstract: Chronic opioid exposure and subsequent abstinence are associated with persistent cognitive impairment and disrupted neuroplasticity, which may be further aggravated by opioid-induced hypogonadism. Brain-derived neurotrophic factor (BDNF) is a key regulator of neuronal plasticity in memory-related brain regions; however, the combined effects of exercise intensity and testosterone replacement during morphine abstinence remain poorly understood. This study investigated whether mild- and moderate-intensity treadmill exercise, alone or in combination with testosterone replacement, could ameliorate cognitive deficits and restore BDNF levels in morphine-abstinent castrated male rats. Rats underwent sham surgery or bilateral castration, followed by a 30-day recovery period, induction of morphine dependence (10 mg/kg, twice daily for 10 days), and a 28-day intervention consisting of sedentary conditions or treadmill exercise with or without testosterone treatment. Spatial learning and memory were evaluated using the Morris water maze, and avoidance memory was assessed using the shuttle box task. BDNF levels in the hippocampus, prefrontal cortex, and serum were quantified by ELISA. Morphine abstinence and castration impaired spatial learning, spatial memory, and avoidance memory and significantly reduced hippocampal and prefrontal cortex BDNF levels. Both mild- and moderate-intensity exercise improved cognitive performance and increased hippocampal and prefrontal cortex BDNF levels, with moderate-intensity exercise generally producing greater benefits. Testosterone replacement partially ameliorated the adverse effects of castration and improved selected behavioral and neurochemical outcomes, although its effects varied across experimental conditions. These findings suggest that appropriately prescribed exercise is an effective non-pharmacological strategy for promoting cognitive recovery and restoring neurotrophic signaling during morphine abstinence, while testosterone replacement may provide additional benefit under hypogonadal conditions.

title: Increases in a pivotal bioactive peptide in specific brain regions reflect the progression of pathology in Alzheimer's disease.
abstract: Abnormal activation of a developmental process driven by a bioactive peptide T14, is posited as a key mechanism in the degeneration of the primarily vulnerable nuclei during the prodromal phase of Alzheimer's Disease (AD). We use a range of anatomical, biochemical and genetic approaches to explore changes in T14 and its target, α7nAChR, in AD and in individuals with mood disorders, a frequent prelude to the disease. Using paired samples from the same patients, levels of T14 and α7nAChR increased in the hippocampus across the AD continuum. In contrast, in early Braak stages, T14 levels in the midbrain reach a plateau and are primarily localised to glia. Moreover, in a cognitively healthy cohort, CSF derived ex vivo revealed a differential profile between T14 and tau levels in individuals with mood disorders, a well-known precursor to AD. These observations confirm a key role of T14 in the neuropathology of AD. Finally, we show a Braak-stage dependant and selective increase in an acetylcholinesterase isoform (AChE-R) already associated with AD pathology, where the profile corresponds closely to that of T14, thereby providing further clues regarding its provenance. By highlighting region and cell-specific changes in the T14 profile as AD progresses, this study further validates a key role for T14 in the progression of neurodegeneration. Finally, the mood disorder-dependent changes based on T14 in CSF might reflect dysfunction in the primarily vulnerable isodendritic core and as such be viewed as a possible, albeit non-exclusive, prelude to AD. Collectively, these results underscore the importance of T14 in AD aetiology and could aid the development of precise and effective therapeutics to target its progression.

title: Furin deficiency in excitatory neurons leads to cognitive dysfunction and glutamatergic synaptic impairment.
abstract: Furin, a pivotal member of the proprotein convertase family, exhibits markedly diminished expression in both Alzheimer's disease (AD) patients and animal models. However, the precise mechanisms by which furin regulates AD-associated cognitive impairment have yet to be fully elucidated. In the present study, we generated excitatory neuron-specific Furin conditional knockout (Furin cKO) mice to investigate the effects and underlying mechanisms of furin deficiency on cognitive decline. We further overexpressed furin in excitatory neurons of 5×FAD transgenic AD model mice to explore the neuroprotective capacity of furin. Compared with control littermates, Furin cKO mice displayed significant impairments in spatial memory alongside elevated anxiety-like behaviors, hippocampal atrophy, and blunted hippocampal long-term potentiation (LTP). Mechanistic analyses further revealed that these neurobehavioral and electrophysiological deficits stemmed from marked reductions in dendritic arbor complexity, spine density, and glutamatergic receptor expression throughout the hippocampus and cerebral cortex of Furin cKO mice. Conversely, neuron-specific overexpression of furin in excitatory neurons of 5×FAD transgenic mice exerted promising rescue effects on the cognitive deficits of this AD model. This functional restoration was accompanied by recovered dendritic and synaptic abundance, alleviated Aβ plaque deposition, and reduced reactive glial activation. These data demonstrate that furin expression in excitatory neurons is critical for maintaining intact synaptic plasticity and normal cognitive function. Moreover, our findings indicate that furin likely serves as a promising therapeutic candidate for alleviating pathological progression in AD and other associated neurodegenerative disorders.

title: Sociodemographic and comorbidity factors mediate ethno-racial differences in plasma Alzheimer's disease biomarkers.
abstract: Ethno-racial disparities in Alzheimer's disease (AD) risk are well-documented, yet mechanisms underlying these differences remain poorly understood. This study investigates plasma AD biomarkers reflective of amyloid, tau, neurodegeneration, and inflammation across Hispanic, non-Hispanic Black/ African American, and non-Hispanic White adults, and examines whether social determinants of health (SDOH) and comorbidities mediate observed disparities. Data from the community-based Health and Aging Brain Study - Health Disparities (HABS-HD) included 1,256 Hispanic, 723 Black, and 1,243 non-Hispanic White participants. Group differences in plasma biomarkers (phosphorylated tau-217 [p-tau217], amyloid-β 42/40 ratio [Aβ42/40], phosphorylated tau-181 [p-tau181], total tau, neurofilament light chain [NfL], and glial fibrillary acidic protein [GFAP]) were assessed using ANCOVA adjusted for age, sex, APOE-ε4 status, and cognitive status. Multiple mediation models tested whether social determinants of health (income, education, area deprivation, chronic stress, social support) and comorbidity factors (BMI, creatinine, total cholesterol, HbA1c, systolic blood pressure) mediate group differences, with covariates and mediators considered simultaneously, resulting in 22 mediation models. Significant differences were observed across all plasma biomarkers. Both Black and Hispanic adults showed lower p-tau217 and p-tau181 compared to non-Hispanic White adults (p's < 0.001). Hispanic adults exhibited lower Aβ42/40 compared to both groups (p's < 0.05) and lower GFAP compared to non-Hispanic White adults (p = 0.002), but higher total tau (p's < 0.01) compared to both groups. Hispanics had higher NfL than Black adults (p < 0.001) but did not differ from non-Hispanic Whites, while Black adults had lower NfL than non-Hispanic White adults (p < 0.001). Comorbidity factors, particularly creatinine (10 of 22 models), BMI (8 models), and HbA1c (7 models), consistently mediated biomarker differences. SDOH factors demonstrated mediation for Aβ42/40, p-tau181, and NfL, with area deprivation and education as key mediators. SDOH and comorbidities were associated with plasma AD biomarker differences observed across ethno-racial groups, though their influence varies by biomarker type and comparison group. Renal function (creatinine), metabolic factors (BMI, HbA1c), and structural disadvantages (area deprivation, education) emerged as critical factors. However, many effects remain unexplained, suggesting additional biological, environmental, or unmeasured social factors contribute to disparities. These findings highlight the need for precision medicine approaches that integrate biological, systemic health, and social contexts when interpreting biomarkers and guiding dementia prevention.

title: Internet-based Emotion Regulation Individual Therapy for Adolescents (IERITA) plus treatment as usual versus treatment as usual for adolescent outpatients with non-suicidal self-injury-the TEENS multi-site trial: study protocol and statistical analysis plan for a multi-site randomised clinical trial.
abstract: Non-suicidal self-injury (NSSI) is a public health concern and a widespread behaviour, especially among adolescents. NSSI is an indicator of psychological distress and a known risk factor for later suicidal behaviour and death by suicide; however, evidence-based treatment options and early interventions specifically for NSSI in adolescents are sparse. The aim of the TEENS multi-site randomised clinical trial is to investigate the benefits and harms of the 11-week IERITA programme (Internet-based Emotion Regulation Individual Therapy for Adolescents) added to treatment as usual (TAU) versus TAU alone in 13- to 17-year-old patients with NSSI referred to psychiatric outpatient services in four out of five Danish regions. Here, we present a combined protocol paper and statistical analysis plan for the TEENS multi-site trial. The TEENS multi-site trial is an investigator-initiated, two-arm, parallel-group randomised clinical superiority trial with blinded outcome assessment. IERITA is provided as an add-on treatment to TAU and compared with TAU alone. IERITA is a therapist-guided, internet-delivered intervention for adolescents teaching emotion regulation skills and includes a complementary part for parents. Participants are randomly allocated in a 1:1 ratio, stratified by trial site and past-month NSSI episodes at baseline (1-10 compared to ≥11 episodes). The primary outcome is NSSI episodes within the past month measured by the Deliberate Self-Harm Inventory Youth version (DHSI-Y). Secondary outcomes include quality of life (KIDSCREEN-10), symptoms of depression, anxiety, and stress (DASS-21), and the proportion of participants with any past-month NSSI. Both primary and secondary outcomes are measured at the end of the intervention (12 weeks). Analyses will be conducted according to the intention-to-treat principle. This paper presents the design and statistical analysis plan for the TEENS multi-site trial. Publishing these considerations before inclusion of the last participant helps increase transparency and limit bias. The trial is approved by the Regional Ethics Committee in the Capital Region of Denmark (H-21035306; 1 February 2022, protocol version 1.3) and the Regional Data Protection Agency (P-2020-113; 8 September 2021). The trial is registered on ClinicalTrials.gov (identifier: NCT05179655; 5 January 2022).

title: From selective phases to reversible fibers: context-dependent structural logic of biomolecular condensates.
abstract: Eukaryotic cellular organization relies on precise compartmentalization. A paradigm shift reveals that proteins with low-complexity domains (LCDs) assemble into dynamic, membraneless compartments called biomolecular condensates. Here, we compare the established "selective phase" model of the nuclear pore complex with the "reversible fiber" concept developed from selected RNA granules, proposing a context-dependent, structure-informed view of macromolecular assembly driven by liquid-liquid phase separation (LLPS). We use the "Temperate Zone" as a descriptive heuristic: in selected systems, LCDs form labile, polymeric assemblies that are sufficiently stable for function yet sufficiently weak for regulation and reversal. This "virtue of weakness" can reflect an evolutionary trade-off, balancing self-assembly with safeguards against pathological transitions. Specific architectures, such as polar zippers and kinked β-sheets, can scaffold selected condensates into viscoelastic network fluids, whereas other condensates remain predominantly disordered and acquire viscoelasticity through transient sticker networks without detectable fibers. Importantly, in some systems, this tunable metastability means environmental stress or mutations can trigger pathological liquid-to-solid transitions, forming toxic aggregates; in other systems, disease can arise from failed condensate formation, altered composition, or depletion of a soluble functional pool. We present a synthesis in which deciphering this "molecular grammar" and the resulting material state is key to understanding condensate formation, physiological function, and dysregulation in condensatopathies such as neurodegeneration and cancer.

title: Research on gambling and gambling harm in Aotearoa New Zealand: a scoping review.
abstract: Gambling harm is a significant public health issue made more urgent by the rapid growth of online gambling. In Aotearoa New Zealand, gambling access expanded following the introduction of gaming machines in the 1990s and is expected to expand again with the regulation of online casinos. With online casinos now being regulated, it is timely to examine the local evidence and identify gaps in the research. This study aimed to determine: (i) the focus of peer-reviewed gambling research conducted in New Zealand between 2003 and 2024; (ii) the methodologies used and their adequacy; and (iii) the nature and extent of funding reported in peer-reviewed publications. MEDLINE, PsycINFO and Scopus were searched for peer-reviewed articles published between 2003 and 2024. Articles of any design were eligible if they focused on gambling, gambling harm or problem gambling, were conducted in New Zealand and included at least one New Zealand-based author. A total of 176 articles were included. Research addressed overlapping domains of individual factors (23.3%), epidemiology and harm (18.2%), social and cultural factors (18.8%), community and context (15.3%), screening and treatment (23.3%), and policy and industry regulation (14.8%). Cross-sectional studies were the most common design (37.5%), followed by non-systematic reviews (20.5%) and qualitative studies (13.1%). Only five clinical trials and seven experimental or quasi-experimental studies were identified. Qualitative methods were most common in research addressing social and cultural factors. Among 167 articles reporting funding information, 37% received gambling levy funding, 27% general research funding, 30% reported no funding and 6% received overseas funding; none reported direct gambling-industry funding. New Zealand has produced a substantial body of peer-reviewed gambling research, but relatively little research has tested what works to reduce gambling harm. Major gaps were evaluations of public health and regulatory responses, treatment and prevention outcomes, the effects of gambling on affected others and whānau, online gambling, and culturally grounded responses for Māori, Pacific and Asian communities. The introduction of regulated online casinos increases the need for prospective research that can track changes to gambling and gambling harm and inform policy and regulation.

title: Evaluation of an institutional leadership program's impact on skills and confidence.
abstract: The Career Development for Women Leaders (CDWL) program was developed to enhance leadership skills for mid- and senior-career faculty through monthly sessions addressing leadership topics. Participants completed pre-, post-, and two-year follow-up program surveys, using items from the Executive Leadership in Academic Medicine instrument. Skill and confidence changes (rated 6-7 on a 1-7 scale) were evaluated with logistic mixed models. Participants (N = 212) with immediate post-program data (N = 96) reported significant increases in 34 of 47 skills (72%) and all confidence items (p's 100% relative increase) in self-assessed abilities occurred, including in facilitating group decision-making (401%), negotiating employment (294%), designing effective organizations (282%), and understanding different work styles (170%). CDWL participants self-identified significant improvements in leadership skills and confidence, particularly in decision-making, negotiation, team management, and leadership self-awareness.

title: Anthropometry with a nutritional focus on motor function, hand-grip strength and subjectively assessed fatigue at diagnosis in Parkinson´s disease.
abstract: Altered anthropometry and nutritional status are associated with motor- and non-motor symptoms in patients with Parkinson´s disease (PD). To investigate if anthropometry can discriminate between low and high levels of motor symptoms, hand grip strength (HGS) and fatigue. Cross-sectional study including baseline data on newly diagnosed patients with PD prior to start of anti-Parkinson medication. Assessments of body composition, risk for malnutrition, fatigue severity scale (FSS) and motor symptoms using Unified Parkinson´s Disease Rating Scale (UPDRS III), including gait performance and ability to arise from chair and HGS were performed at diagnosis. Clinical characteristics and anthropometrical variables were compared between patients with or without motor symptoms and low or high level of fatigue or HGS. Logistic regression was used to examine the association between anthropometry and the odds of having motor difficulties or fatigue. Increased body mass index (BMI) was associated with difficulty arising from chair (OR 1.37, 95% CI 1.09, 1.72, p = 0.007). In addition, these patients had low intracellular water index, (5.2 (1.2) vs. 6.4 (0.7) p < 0.001) and fat free mass index (13.9 (2.3) vs. 15.8 (3.1), p = 0.005) and higher fat mass % (42.5 (7.2) vs. 40.2 (9.8), p = 0.024) compared with patients without difficulty. Patients with high FSS had higher UPDRS II (10 (4) vs. 8 (5), p < 0.001), higher BMI (27.9 (3.8) vs. 25.4 (5.7), p = 0.039) and larger calf circumference​ (37.5 (5.0) vs. 35.8 (4.1)), p = 0.045) than patients with low FSS. Low HGS was associated with low mid upper arm circumference (30.0 (4.0) vs. 32.0 (4.0), p < 0.007) and low calf circumference (35.5 (4.4) vs. 37.0 (4.8), p = 0.049), low fat free mass index (14.9 (3.1) vs. 16.0 (3.2)), intracellular water index (5.7 (1.7) vs. 6.4 (1.6), p = 0.004) and arm muscle area (25.5 (3.5) vs. 26.7 (4.3), p = 0.047) as compared with patients with high HGS. Anthropometry could be used to discriminate between level of motor function, HGS and perceived fatigue at diagnosis of PD. The amount of muscle mass and BMI were important when evaluating the clinical condition in patients with difficulty arising from chair or having low HGS as compared with normal function.

title: Reversal of motor dysfunction, memory impairment, anxiety-like behaviour and depression after withdrawal from chronic vanadium neurotoxicity in mice.
abstract: Vanadium, a transition metal widely distributed in the environment, has been involved in neurotoxicity through oxidative stress and neuroinflammation. Chronic exposure may impair motor function, cognition, anxiety and depression-like behaviours, but the potential for recovery after withdrawal remains unclear especially in motor function, anxiety and depression-like behaviours. Male BALB/c mice were exposed to sodium metavanadate (3 mg/kg, intraperitoneal) for 3-, 9- or 15-months. Withdrawal groups received vanadium for 3-months followed by 6- or 12-months without exposure. Neurobehavioural assessments included motor coordination (inverted grid, beam walking), cognitive function (Y-maze), anxiety-like behaviour (open field) and depression-like behaviour (tail suspension test). Track and heat maps were used to visualize exploration and activity patterns. Chronic vanadium exposure induced progressive deficits in motor coordination, spatial memory, anxiety-like behaviour and depressive-like states. These impairments were most pronounced at 15-months of exposure. Withdrawal groups demonstrated partial recovery after 6-months and near-complete restoration after 12-months, with neurobehavioural performance approaching control levels across domains. Chronic vanadium exposure impairs motor, cognitive and affective functions in mice, but withdrawal promotes recovery, highlighting the reversibility of vanadium-induced neurotoxicity. These findings draw attention to the risks of chronic vanadium exposure while offering evidence that cessation can mitigate long-term neurobehavioural impairments.

title: Trajectories of Sleep and Pain From the Perioperative Period to One-Year After Knee Arthroplasty: A Prospective Cohort Study.
abstract: Poor sleep quality and pain are closely related, and surgery is known to impair sleep quality temporarily. Yet the effects of daily fluctuations in sleep and pain and their impact on long-term outcomes remain insufficiently explored. This prospective cohort study explored bidirectional day-to-day associations between sleep and pain and preoperative predictors of one-year pain outcomes. A total of 171 patients with osteoarthritis scheduled for knee arthroplasty were enrolled. Preoperative assessments included sleep quality, symptoms of anxiety and depression, lifestyle evaluation, and pain intensity. For the first week after surgery, patients reported daily sleep quality and pain intensity. After 1 year, knee pain intensity was reassessed. One hundred and twenty-five patients completed preoperative assessments, 89 completed all seven postoperative daily assessments, and 112 responded after 1 year. Pain peaked on postoperative day two and was significantly lower than preoperative levels at 1 year (p < 0.05). Daily fluctuations in pain and sleep were bidirectionally correlated: higher pain intensity predicted poorer sleep quality the following night (p < 0.05), while poor sleep quality predicted higher next-day pain intensities (p < 0.05). Patients in the worst quartiles of pain and sleep during the first postoperative week reported significantly higher one-year postoperative pain compared to those in the best quartiles (p < 0.05). Preoperative positive affect, with non-significant contributions from sleep quality and symptoms of anxiety, predicted 13.1% (adjusted R2 10.2%) of the variance in one-year postoperative pain. In conclusion, sleep, pain, and psychological factors in the perioperative period are relevant for long-term pain outcomes after knee arthroplasty.

title: Peptide-mediated nanotheranostics for glioblastoma.
abstract: Glioblastoma multiforme (GBM) is the most aggressive primary brain tumor in adults, with limited therapeutic efficacy and poor clinical outcomes. A major obstacle to effective treatment and molecular imaging is the blood-brain barrier (BBB), which severely restricts the delivery of therapeutic agents and imaging probes to the tumor microenvironment. BBB-penetrating and tumor-targeting peptides have emerged as versatile molecular platforms that can facilitate BBB transport, enhance tumor accumulation, and improve the delivery of therapeutic and diagnostic cargos. This review provides a comprehensive overview of the development of BBB-penetrating and GBM-targeting peptides, focusing on their sources, screening strategies, and underlying transport mechanisms. Representative peptides, including Angiopep-2, mApoE, T7, RVG, cRGD, and iRGD, are discussed in the context of drug delivery and molecular imaging applications. Recent advances in artificial intelligence and machine-learning approaches are highlighted as complementary strategies for accelerating peptide discovery and optimizing candidate selection, while emphasizing the necessity of experimental validation. Preclinical studies demonstrate that peptide functionalization can improve BBB permeability, tumor targeting, intratumoral distribution, and imaging performance in various delivery systems. Early clinical translation has been explored through peptide-drug conjugates, chlorotoxin-based imaging agents and cellular therapies, RGD-based radiotracers, and peptide vaccines; however, clinical evidence remains preliminary and variable across platforms. Key challenges limiting broader application include peptide instability, receptor heterogeneity, off-target clearance, protein-corona formation, and formulation-dependent biological performance. Overall, peptide-mediated delivery and nanotheranostics platforms represent a promising strategy to overcome BBB limitations and advance precision diagnosis and treatment of GBM. Future progress will require integrated optimization of peptide engineering, delivery systems, imaging technologies, and rigorous clinical validation to achieve reliable and scalable translation.

title: PROTECT: PRegnancy Outcomes using continuous glucose monitoring TEChnology in pregnant women with early-onset Type 2 diabetes: a multicentre randomised controlled trial - study protocol.
abstract: Early-onset type 2 diabetes (EOT2D), meaning type 2 diabetes diagnosed before the age of 40 disproportionately affects women from socially deprived and minority ethnic groups. EOT2D is now the most common form of pre-existing diabetes complicating pregnancy. These pregnancies carry high risks of congenital anomalies, stillbirth, neonatal death, and of both maternal and neonatal morbidity. Maternal glycaemia is the key modifiable risk factor yet remains suboptimal and is often accompanied by limited self-monitoring of blood glucose (SMBG). Continuous Glucose Monitoring (CGM) offers continuous real-time glucose profiles, potentially enabling better dietary, lifestyle and therapy adjustments. The PROTECT trial is a multicentre, randomised controlled trial designed to evaluate whether CGM improves maternal glucose and neonatal outcomes in women with EOT2D. The trial will recruit 422 pregnant participants (≤ 16 weeks 0 days' gestation, HbA1c ≥ 43 mmol/mol) from around 20 UK NHS antenatal diabetes clinics. After a run-in phase with masked CGM, participants will be randomised to either real-time CGM (FreeStyle Libre 3) or standard SMBG. The primary maternal outcome is percentage of time in pregnancy-specific glucose target range (3.5-7.8 mmol/L). The primary neonatal outcome is a composite of neonatal care unit admission or death. Secondary outcomes include maternal HbA1c, glycaemic variability, insulin use, obstetric complications, neonatal morbidity, psychosocial measures, and cost-effectiveness. An internal pilot will assess recruitment feasibility, before proceeding to the full trial. Qualitative interviews with women and healthcare professionals will explore barriers and facilitators to CGM use. Statistical analyses will follow intention-to-treat principles. This is the largest trial to date investigating CGM in EOT2D pregnancy, aiming to generate robust evidence on clinical efficacy, lived experiences, and economic impact, informing future NHS policy and practice. ISRCTN12804317 Registration Date: 23/10/2023.

title: Machine learning prediction model of transition from acute kidney injury to acute kidney disease after liver transplantation: a retrospective study.
abstract: The transition from acute kidney injury (AKI) to acute kidney disease (AKD) is a frequent sequela after liver transplantation (LT), associated with increased short-term mortality, prolonged hospitalization, and increased likelihood of progression to chronic kidney disease. Early identification of high-risk patients remains a critical unmet need. This study aimed to develop a machine learning-based model for early prediction of AKI-to-AKD transition after LT. Patients who underwent LT and developed postoperative AKI between January 2019 and December 2022 were enrolled as the development cohort (n = 359), randomly allocated into a training set and an internal validation set. Six machine learning algorithms were evaluated to construct prediction models. All models were subsequently assessed in a temporal validation cohort in the same medical center (n = 104 from January 2024 to December 2025). The Shapley Additive Explanations (SHAP) were used for model interpretation. An online risk calculator was developed based on the final model. The incidence of postoperative AKD in the training set was 57.1%. AKD progression was associated with 8 predictors: postoperative day 7 blood urea nitrogen (BUN), preoperative serum creatinine (Scr), postoperative day 7 sodium, calcineurin inhibitor overexposure, imipenem/cilastatin use, amphotericin B use, sex, and cefoperazone/sulbactam use. The logistic regression model demonstrated the best overall performance, with an AUC of 0.805 in the internal validation cohort and 0.809 in the temporal validation cohort, with good calibration. SHAP analysis indicated that postoperative BUN, preoperative Scr, and postoperative sodium were the most influential predictors. Decision curve analysis demonstrated net clinical benefit. This study developed and temporally validated an interpretable predictive model for AKI-to-AKD transition after LT, which can facilitate early identification of high-risk patients and guide individualized nephroprotective strategies.

title: Urolithin A mitigates behavioural and synaptic deficits associated with epilepsy.
abstract: The persistence of drug-resistant epilepsy highlights the need for new therapies that target novel mechanisms while maintaining synaptic strength and minimizing side effects. Small molecules of natural origin with anti-epileptogenic potential can influence altered synaptic deficits and reducing seizure threshold, offering a strategy to restore cellular energy homeostasis and slow the progression of epilepsy and associated comorbidities. We used a combination of approaches including behavioural assays, immunostaining and electrophysiological recordings to study the synaptic contributions to reduced seizure-threshold in both Drosophila and mouse models of epilepsy. In addition, we used affinity-purification with synthesized beads specific for our small molecule to identify its cellular partners. We found that administration of Urolithin-A (UA), a small molecule of natural origin, mitigated behavioural and synaptic dysfunctions under chemically and genetically induced epileptic conditions in Drosophila. Additionally, chronic treatment with UA attenuated the altered single-cell and network synaptic transmission in PTZ-induced chronic kindling of mice. However, UA exerted no seizure-suppressive effects in in vitro epileptic conditions, suggesting the absence of acute anti-epileptic effects. In addition, we identified the direct interactor of UA as the complex of tubulin dimer and VDAC1. Molecular docking analyses also predicted that urolithin A interacts with VDAC1. Consistent with the neuroprotective role of VDAC1 downregulation reported in previous studies, neuron-specific knockdown of VDAC1 in Drosophila phenocopied the effects of UA. Collectively, our data show that UA exerts disease-modifying anti-epileptic effects in both Drosophila and mouse models with VDAC1 identified as a critical functional mediator; however, direct functional modulation of VDAC1 and associated partners by UA will require further experimental validation. These findings provide the blueprint for future drug discovery targeting VDAC1-dependent pathways.

title: Intracranial metastases in sarcoma: a (not so) rare localization, experience of a sarcoma reference center.
abstract: Intracranial metastases (IM) in patients with soft tissue sarcomas (STS) and bone sarcomas (BS) are uncommon. The reported incidence ranges from 1% to 3%, although it varies according to histological subtype, with alveolar soft part sarcoma and Ewing sarcoma showing the highest propensity for central nervous system (CNS) involvement. The development of IM is associated with a poor prognosis. We conducted a single-center retrospective study including patients with STS and BS treated at the Veneto Institute of Oncology between 2010 and 2024. Data collected included age at diagnosis, sex, primary tumor characteristics, date and site of first metastasis, time to IM, and radiological characteristics of IM (number, location, and presence of peritumoral edema). Information on neurological symptoms, treatment strategies, and survival outcomes was also retrieved. Overall survival (OS) was estimated using the Kaplan-Meier method. Among 1,870 patients, including 801 with advanced disease, 30 developed IM, corresponding to an overall incidence of 1.6% and 3.7% among patients with advanced disease. The most frequent histological subtypes were Ewing sarcoma (16.7%), undifferentiated pleomorphic sarcoma (16.7%), and chondrosarcoma (13.3%). The median time from sarcoma diagnosis to IM was 30 months, while the median interval from the onset of metastatic disease to IM was 7 months. Most IM were diagnosed following the onset of neurological symptoms (70%), which were more commonly related to lesion location than to intracranial hypertension. The cerebrum was the most frequent site of involvement (66.7%), followed by the meninges (20.0%) and cerebellum (13.3%). Overall, 23 patients (76.7%) received at least one treatment for IM: 40.0% underwent local treatment alone, 20.0% received systemic therapy alone, and 30.0% received a combination of local and systemic treatments. Among patients receiving local treatment, radiotherapy alone was administered in 57.2% of cases, surgery alone in 21.4%, and combined surgery and radiotherapy in 21.4%. At the time of analysis, 25 of the 30 patients had died. Median OS after IM diagnosis was 2 months (95% CI, 1.14-2.85). In this single-center series of patients with STS and BS, the overall incidence of IM was low, although certain histological subtypes showed a higher risk of CNS involvement. Most IM were solitary and potentially amenable to local treatment. Despite multimodal management, IM remained associated with a dismal prognosis. Further studies are needed to better understand the biological mechanisms underlying CNS dissemination and to identify more effective therapeutic strategies.

title: Does succinic acid treatment improve metabolic health in a male murine model of early ageing?
abstract: Ageing associates with obesity, mitochondrial dysfunction, and impaired glucose homeostasis. Previously, we documented that succinic acid (SA) treatment improves mitochondrial function and adiposity; however, the effects on ageing are unknown. Therefore, we determined the effect of SA treatment on metabolic health in 19 aged male mice (Age; 16 months), randomized to receive vehicle (Veh, n = 8) or SA (n = 11) and compared to young controls (Young; 6 months) (n = 24). After 6 weeks of treatment, insulin tolerance (IT), glucose tolerance (GT), pyruvate tolerance (PT) and physical activity (PA) were assessed. Body mass (BM), epididymal white adipose tissue (EWAT) and heart mass (HM) were measured at study end. Soleus muscle and EWAT underwent mitochondrial respirometry.
